offer.say: Okay. Don't freak out. There's a girl from Port Ainsley with a 1988 Millbrook Peewee B pin. 1988! Same as the pennant! She'll trade it for one thing. This year's host pin. You have a host pin. I know you have a host pin. Bob gave it to you. Everybody knows.

options.text: You can have it. Make the trade.
I'm keeping the host pin, Tommy.

why.say: They won the valley! Peewee B! The pennant's in the trophy case, bottom shelf, by the pike. There were only forty pins made. Only six left in the world. Probably. I made that number up. But it's rare.

cheek.say: The satisfaction of a good trade. And my respect. My respect is worth a lot. It's worth at least a Kessler Atom A.

options.text: Deal. Your respect and a trade.

decline.say: That's fair. It's a good pin. I'd keep it too. I'm not crying, it's the rink air.

accepted.say: YES. Okay. Bring it to the table. Don't wear it in, it devalues it.

options.text: Coming to look at the table.
You've got the pin. When's the trade?

p_trade.say: Next tournament. She's coming back with her team. Her team's terrible, but her pins are amazing.

complete.say: I got it. 1988 Peewee B. It's real. It's got the old crest with the moose that looks like a dog. And I thought about it a lot and I think it should be yours. Not mine. The rink's.

options.text: Then it goes in the trophy case, next to the pennant.
You keep it, Tommy. You earned it.
Does the moose really look like a dog?

c_case.say: Next to the pennant! With a label! Can the label say 'traded by Tommy B.'? Small. In the corner.

c_keep.say: Really? Really really? I'm going to wear it. No. I'm going to frame it. No. Both.

c_moose.say: It's a dog. Everyone knows it's a dog. The artist's dog, probably. They never fixed it. It's better as a dog.

done.say: Next tournament I'm going for the Kessler 1979. Nobody's ever seen one.
